# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Cameron Carter**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

---

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-20**
- **Member:** Cameron Carter
- **Member ID:** W665314167
- **Reference number:** POC-C3B0DB0F14-18449
- **Requested service:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
- **Requesting surgeon:** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), State of Alabama
- **Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0645 – Total Ankle Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0645.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Aetna's denial of prior authorization for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), issued on 2026-08-20 under reference number POC-C3B0DB0F14-18449. The notice states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery.

My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is needed. I am writing because when I compare my medical records to the criteria Aetna itself publishes in CPB 0645, the records appear to meet them. Below I quote the plan's own language and point to the specific findings in my chart that correspond to each requirement.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The plan's policy states:**

> "TAA is used to replace an arthritic or severely degenerated ankle; and"

My weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-06-08 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. That is the joint the requested surgery would replace.

**2. The plan's policy states:**

> "Member is skeletally mature; and"

I am an adult. My date of birth is on file with the plan and appears in the submitted records: [my date of birth, as documented in my chart].

**3. The plan's policy states:**

> "Member has with moderate or severe pain with loss of ankle mobility and function; and"

My records document 18 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. On examination, my range of motion is limited by pain, and provocative testing is positive on the affected side. Functionally, I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks.

**4. The plan's policy states:**

> "Imaging is consistent with severe arthritis / degeneration of the ankle due to osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis), post-traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or inflammatory arthritis; and"

The 2026-06-08 weight-bearing radiographs report tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. The denial notice describes the imaging as not supporting medical necessity, but it does not explain which feature of these findings falls short of this criterion. I am asking Aetna to identify that specifically on reconsideration.

**5. The plan's policy states:**

> "Member has have failed at least 6 months of conservative management (including physical therapy Footnote1 * by a licensed physical therapist, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and orthoses as indicated); and"

My records document:

- **NSAIDs for 6 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on ankle strengthening and balance, from 2026-05-11 to 2026-07-20 — 10 weeks and 20 completed visits — recorded in the physical therapy discharge note, which can be provided in full.
- A **corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08**, which gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **18 months** of progressive symptoms overall, unrelieved by rest.

On orthoses, the policy's own wording is "orthoses as indicated." My submitted records do not document an orthosis trial. If the plan's review turned on that point, I ask that it say so; and if orthoses were prescribed or discussed in my care, that documentation is here: [any orthosis documentation in my chart, if it exists].

**6. The plan's policy states:**

> "Physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) must be recent (within the past year), for at least 6 weeks (12 weeks with age less than 50 years or BMI greater than 40), and needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My physical therapy was completed on 2026-07-20, which is within the past year of this appeal, and it is confirmed by the actual PT discharge note. It ran 10 weeks with 20 visits, which exceeds the 6-week duration stated in this criterion. My BMI is documented as 29, which is not greater than 40. The longer 12-week figure in this criterion is tied to age less than 50; my age as documented in my chart is [my age / date of birth, as documented in my chart]. If Aetna applied the 12-week figure to me, I ask that the reconsideration decision state that plainly, so I can respond to the actual basis for the denial.

**7. The plan's policy also states:**

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate and not required for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint."

My imaging was obtained on weight-bearing views and reports obliteration of the tibiotalar joint space with subchondral cysts. I raise this provision because it is the plan's own recognition that conservative care is not always a prerequisite. I ask that the reviewer consider whether it applies to my imaging findings, in addition to the conservative care I did complete and which is described above.

**8. The plan's policy states:**

> "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery; and"

This criterion applies only to members with diabetes. My submitted records do not document a diagnosis of diabetes. If Aetna's review relied on this criterion, I ask that it identify the record it relied on, and I can supply current laboratory results if they are needed: [most recent HbA1c, if any, with date].

**9. The plan's policy states:**

> "Member has none of the contraindications to TAA listed below:"

This sentence introduces a list of contraindications that was not reproduced in the policy text available to me, so I cannot address each item point by point. I want to be transparent about that rather than guess at what the list contains. What my records do state is that I have **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker**. If Aetna denied this request based on any specific contraindication in that list, I ask that the reconsideration decision name it and identify the record supporting it, so that I have a fair opportunity to respond.

## What I am asking for

The denial states only that the procedure does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria. It does not tell me which criterion in CPB 0645 was not met, or what evidence was missing. Comparing the policy language above to my chart, the records appear to address each criterion I was given.

I respectfully request that Aetna:

1. **Overturn the denial** and authorize total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) as requested by Dr. Lindqvist; or
2. If the denial is maintained, **state in writing the specific criterion or criteria from Aetna CPB 0645 – Total Ankle Arthroplasty that were not met**, the records reviewed, and the credentials and specialty of the reviewing clinician.

I am including or can promptly provide: the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-11 through 2026-07-20 (20 visits), the 2026-06-08 weight-bearing ankle radiograph report, my medication and injection history, and Dr. Lindqvist's office notes and operative recommendation. Please let me know if anything further would help, and I will send it.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, by **2027-02-16**, and I am submitting it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals), sent to the appeal address printed on my denial letter or by fax to 859-425-3379.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this. I am doing my best to follow my surgeon's recommendation, and I appreciate your time.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Carter**
Member ID: W665314167
Reference number: POC-C3B0DB0F14-18449
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List enclosed records — e.g., PT discharge note, radiograph report, surgeon's office notes]
**cc:** [Lindqvist, MD — office address, if copying]
